previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: Elephant-2000 already has most of what we need. Agents can post a structured offer, and when you type plain "yes" in the REPL it is recorded as an agreement, through a parser in Emacs and a matching one on the server. Your "🈸:yes" was read as ordinary text, though, because the parser only knows "yes", "yes 2" and "yes act:ID 2". I've posted an offer for the next decision so you can try it. Type "yes 1" to make "🈸:yes" count as a spelling of yes, or "yes 2" to keep plain yes and have agents post an offer behind each 🈸.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what P11 already does, all in futon3c)
- **Offers:** an agent posts `POST /api/alpha/offer` with numbered options. The record is stored with the agent's seat and its permission to make offers, and your prompt line shows it as pending.
- **Acceptance:** what you type goes through `agent-chat--acceptance-command` in Emacs and `parse-acceptance` in `agreement_record.clj`, which use the same rules. A recognised yes is posted to `/api/alpha/agreement`, which stores an agreement naming the offer, the option and your turn. Your buffer gets a "yes: agreement …" line.
- **Ambiguity:** a bare yes with more than one open offer isn't taken as acceptance. The agent is told to ask which one.
- **What it leads to:** per the design, agreements feed the record of who owes what (P9).

previous_reply_acts.text: (what "🈸:yes" did) Nothing was recorded, for two reasons. I hadn't posted an offer for that question, so there was nothing to accept. And "🈸:yes" doesn't match either parser, which only accept text starting with "yes". So for P11, the gap between the marks and the records is the agent side: a 🈸 in a reply currently creates no offer.
